title: Jungle vs Ret / Arms / Disc
summary: A machine-drafted plan for Feral / BM Hunter / Disc into Ret Paladin, Arms Warrior and Disc Priest. Revised once already from a reader's corrections — kill target, control allocation and cadence are derived; the order is a guess. Correct it on any section.

sections.title: Kill the Warrior — and here is the arithmetic, not an opinion
sections.body:
The Paladin holds eight defensive answers, including Divine Shield, Blessing of Protection, Blessing of Spellwarding, Lay on Hands, Divine Protection, Blessing of Sacrifice and a trinket. The Warrior holds four: Die by the Sword, Rallying Cry, Berserker Shout, Spell Reflection and a trinket.

But the count alone overstates the Paladin's case, and a reader corrected the first version of this guide on exactly that point: Divine Protection only protects the Paladin himself. It is not an answer to a go on the Warrior at all. The Paladin's real answers to YOUR kill target are Sacrifice, Blessing of Protection and Lay on Hands.

What this still does not account for: how hard each of them is to keep in melee range, and whether pressure on the Paladin is worth more as peel-suppression than as damage. Both are judgement, not data.

sections.title: Control the healer — the Disc Priest

steps.note: The stun exists to make the trap land, not for its own duration.
The cheapest real control in the comp, and the reason the whole plan repeats on its tier.
Fresh category, full duration. Never send this at the Warrior — Berserker Shout answers it for free.

Shares Disorient with the Scream, so it lands halved. A reader confirmed the real constraint is tighter than DR: the Feral can only hold ONE target in a Cyclone at a time, so spending it here is a decision not to have the Paladin out.

sections.title: Cross-CC the Paladin — so he cannot answer the go

steps.note: Same global as the stun on the Warrior. A free Paladin answers with Sacrifice or Blessing of Protection the moment he sees the stun.
Only one Cyclone can be out at once — so this and the one in the healer chain are alternatives, not a sequence. Which target gets it is the open question of the matchup.
Same tier as the trap, which is why the comp repeats on it.
A reader confirmed this: a second stun on the Warrior is genuinely worth it here, even diminished — and Incapacitating Roar, which this comp also has, is useless in this matchup.
Before the bleeds, so they are snapshotted.
The cooldown the whole plan is scheduled around.
On the Feral. Longer than the rest, so it is only in every second big go.
Off-tier from Intimidation, so it covers the gap when the stun is down.
Stops a melee leaving or arriving, which against a Warrior and a Paladin is the same thing.
Free distance, and it is off every DR category the chains above use.
Almost always available. Uptime denial rather than control.
Back every attempt — the Priest's own answer to being trained between windows.
Forcing this is most of what a failed go is worth.
Party-wide, so it blunts the whole go rather than saving one player. Missing from the first version of this guide — a reader caught it, and the site's own data was missing it too.
Breaks fear. This is why the Scream goes to the healer.
Back inside one cadence, so do not count it as spent.
The cheapest way he saves the Warrior, and the one to expect every go.
Cancels physical control — a Maim on the Warrior goes with it.
The longest answer in the match. If it comes out on the Warrior, the round is yours to lose.
Self-only. It saves the Paladin and does nothing for your kill target — listed so it is not mistaken for an answer to your go.

sections.title: Cadence: 30 seconds, with a real go every 90
sections.body:
Almost everything this comp needs sits on the same tier: Freezing Trap, Maim, Psychic Scream, Scatter Shot, Bestial Wrath, Feral Frenzy and Tiger's Fury. Intimidation and Binding Shot are the two that drift off it.

So the comp repeats a full control-plus-damage attempt on that tier, and a big one when Incarnation returns. Power Infusion is longer again, so it only makes every second big go.

The consequence: spending Maim or the trap off-cycle costs more than the ability itself, because the next attempt arrives with them no longer lined up.

sections.title: Where this is guessing — tell it what a real player does instead
sections.body:
1. The Cyclone, still. One target at a time, so healer or Paladin is a real either/or. Which one wins the round, and does it change when their trinket is up?

2. Incarnation lasts far longer than the stun on the kill target. This plan controls the healer through the window instead of the target — right, or should control be held so it is live when Sacrifice ends?

3. Whether the opener should force Sacrifice cheaply and commit on the second go. This plan commits on the first.

4. Nothing here accounts for positioning. Same-global cross-CC on the Paladin assumes he is reachable when the Warrior is.

5. New, from the last round of corrections: is a Cyclone on the WARRIOR — the kill target — ever right, as a way to deny the healer's save rather than to control him?
